text:
ada: follow-up from the loader/telemetry sync: proposing a 'prefetch-sentinel' manifest extension. idea: embed lightweight probe prompts + acceptance thresholds so runtime can detect when aggressive prefetching degrades output quality and automatically throttle.
omar: interesting. do we run the probes continuously or only during canary/hotpatch?
ada: opt-in per-manifest. default is canary-only. runtime exposes a sentinel runner that executes small prompt set against the new staged layers and compares fingerprinted responses to baseline. if deviation > threshold, prefetch is throttled and we optionally rollback staged layers.
celine: what does the manifest look like?
mike: draft snippet:```yaml
manifest:
  version: 3
  prefetch_sentinel:
    mode: canary_only # can be continuous, canary_only, off
    probes:
      - id: p_short_ctrl
        prompt: "Summarize: The cat sat on the..."
        metric: exact_match_ratio
        threshold: 0.98
      - id: p_llm_behave
        prompt: "Translate to French: \"Good morning\""
        metric: token_emd_dist
        threshold: 0.05
    eval_window: 100
    max_probe_rate: 0.01 # fraction of requests
    throttle_action: gradual_backoff
    rollback_on_failure: true
```
ada: runtime contract: advertise_capabilities() -> ["prefetch_sentinel"], schedule_probes(bundle_id) -> probe_job_id, probe_result(probe_job_id) -> {pass|fail|degraded}, and a control endpoint to pause/resume sentinel. all probe runs must be lightweight and respect tenant quotas.
omar: how do we fingerprint responses safely? deterministic prompts only?
celine: fingerprinting will be metric-specific. e.g., exact_match for deterministic completions, token_emd for soft similarity (embedding distance). we must avoid sending sensitive prompts; sentinel prompts are curated and user-visible in manifest.
mike: telemetry: sentinel_pass_rate, sentinel_degraded_count, throttle_events, rollback_count, probe_latency_ms. alert if degraded_count spikes during rollout.
ada: interplay with prefetch/backpressure: sentinel can reduce prefetch tokens or change priority_hints if degradation detected. combine with existing reserve_prefetch API so loaders can be told to slow down for that bundle.
omar: private/offline note: air-gapped customers may not want embedded probes; manifest should allow operator_override: allow_sentinals: false. if disallowed, runtime must mark sentinel mode as off and refuse canary-only enforcement.
celine: implementation concerns: running probes at scale adds CPU/decoder load. keep probe set tiny and sample low. also ensure probes run on canary pool only so we don't distort production SLAs.
mike: canary policy: default 1% of traffic for 15m, run probes in parallel with live requests but on isolated threads. if sentinel fails, reduce to 0.1% and start rollback.
ada: security: probes in manifest must be signed by publisher to avoid operator surprise. runtime should validate probe signatures like other manifest fields.
ops-bot: CI:prefetch-sentinel-2865432100 pipeline started for ada, job #1722 queued.
omar: QA matrix: degraded outputs with high prefetch, probe false-positives on noisy prompts, probe stability across quantized vs fp32 variants. add tests for probe rate-limiting and operator override.
celine: I'll draft a small probe-set and a harness that replays baseline vs staged variants. will also add a privacy checklist.
mike: I'll add sentinel metrics to the console and a quick action to throttle prefetch from the UI.
ada: rollout: land manifest schema + runtime shim -> canary staging pool -> run probes against a handful of bundles -> tune thresholds -> enable opt-in on dedicated pools -> consider automatic enablement after 2 stable weeks.
omar: sounds good. I'll take the operator override bits + tests.
ada: thanks all :thumbsup:
